---
title: "track"
output: html_document
comment: "This file tracks the priority of the parameters by creating a histogram for each
          parameter and seeing how many ups and downs(need to get down to zero) there are for             each bins. The more there are, the more diverse the species are." 
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
#library setup
```

#Read data
```{r}
folder = "simulation/2025_10_22_12_01/SummaryIndividuals"
files <- list.files(folder, pattern = "^SummaryIndividuals_.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
nums <- as.numeric(gsub("\\D", "", basename(files)))
files <- files[order(nums)]
world <- lapply(files, read.csv)
world <- do.call(rbind, world)
```

#List of parameters (isLight and parentIsLigt are categorical, rest are numerical)
```{r}
param_list <- c("lifeSpan", "speed", "maxEnergy", "kidEnergy", "sensors", "nkids", "pgmDeath", "matForKids", "energy")
```

#Iterate one each and count the number of different 
```{r}
set.seed(1) 
sampled_world <- world[sample(nrow(world), 1000, replace = FALSE), ]


for(param in param_list){
  title = paste("Distribution of", param)
  hist(sampled_world[[param]], breaks = 20, main= title, xlab=param, ylab="Frequency")
}
```
